title: Raft in four rules
purpose: Connect replication, commitment, elections and availability into one picture.
sequence_reason: The four rules build on each other: replication feeds commitment, and elections restore replication after a failure.
summary: A recap of Raft: the leader appends and replicates log entries, an entry commits once a majority stores it, a failed leader is replaced by an election that needs a majority of votes, and without a majority the cluster stops rather than give wrong answers.
explanation: Every Raft rule uses the same majority, so any two majorities share a server, and that shared server carries the committed history forward.

learning_check.question: Why does using a majority for both commits and elections keep committed entries safe?
learning_check.answer: Any two majorities of the same cluster share at least one server, so the voters for a new leader include a server that stores every committed entry.

scenes.heading: Why majorities keep data safe
scenes.narration: A commit majority and an election majority of five always share at least one server. That server carries every committed entry into the next term.
